data.name: Samaira
data.gender_notes: Samaira is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Samaira is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘समयारा’ (samayara), which means 'Goddess of Prosperity'. It is believed that this name bestows wealth, prosperity, and abundance. Samaira is also associated with the goddess Lakshmi, who is the deity of wealth and fortune. The name Samaira carries the meaning “Goddess of Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Samaira usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Samaira belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Samaira total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Samaira holds significant cultural importance in Hindu traditions, symbolizing prosperity and abundance. In Hindu mythology, the goddess Lakshmi, who is revered for her blessings of wealth, prosperity, and fortune, is often invoked to ensure abundance in all areas of life. Samaira, being associated with the goddess, carries the blessings of Lakshmi in terms of material successes, financial stability, and abundance.
data.spiritual_significance: Samaira, as a spiritual name, embodies the divine energies of abundance, prosperity, and wealth, bestowing blessings of both material wealth and spiritual growth. It encourages the bearer to live a life of contentment, generosity, and gratitude, reminding them of the infinite blessings that the universe holds for them. Additionally, Samaira signifies the innate ability to enjoy the fruits of life, appreciate the spiritual journey, and remain steadfast in the pursuit of self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Samaira: The radiant one who embodies the pure and unwavering devotion towards the divine, constantly seeking inner enlightenment and striving towards self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Samaira was a prominent Jain monk and philosopher who lived during the 12th century in India. He was a disciple of Hemachandra, the founder of the Digambara Terapanthi sect, and is known for his contributions to Jain literature and philosophy.

Samaira is also mentioned in the Puranic literature of Hinduism, specifically in the 'Skanda Purana', as a princess of the Haihayas, a royal dynasty in ancient India. She was the wife of Bhagadatta, a powerful king of Anga, and is known for her piety and devotion towards Lord Shiva.
